subject: Private GPU pool — burst containment & bi-modal scaling plan
messages:
From: Beth Dunlop <beth.dunlop@acme-corp.com>

Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private GPU pool sizing — baseline vs spikes (Q1 load samples attached)

Karthik,

Thanks again for taking this call earlier. Attached are a compressed set of request traces (acme_load_profile_q1.csv) and a quick PNG of our on-prem network layout. We want your recommendation for provisioning a private GPU pool that covers:

- A stable baseline: sustained 350 tokens/sec for our user-facing embeddings+chat workloads (regional), 24/7.
- Short spikes: up to 10x above baseline for up to 10 minutes, occurring ~6 times/day during marketing pushes.

Constraints to consider:
- Our on-prem switching has 25 Gbps leaf uplinks; we want to avoid cross-rack egress saturation.
- We use a NAT cluster with 4096 SNAT ports per appliance; past spikes have caused port exhaustion and failed outbound telemetry during peak bursts.
- Security requires private control plane and no public IP on workers.

Primary asks:
1) A capacity plan that keeps 95th/99th token latency under 400ms at baseline and under 1s during spikes (with graceful degradation).
2) Clear autoscale + warmup recipe to avoid cold KV cache penalty for first requests in a burst.
3) Network mitigations to prevent SNAT exhaustion and avoid cross-rack egress thrash.

I've cc'd our ops address. Happy to hop on a working session.

Thanks,
Beth Dunlop
Head of ML Ops, Acme Corp

Attachment stubs: acme_load_profile_q1.csv (CSV, 1.2MB), privfarm_network_map.png (PNG, 420KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — baseline vs spikes (Q1 load samples attached)

Beth — thanks for the traces and the network diagram. High level thoughts up front, then proposed next steps below.

Summary (short):
- Target topology: a bi-modal fleet (baseline steady-nodes + pre-warmed burst ring). Baseline handles 24/7 load; burst ring is a small set of pre-warmed hosts kept ready for fast scale to absorb 6x-10x spikes without cold-start penalties.
- Network mitigations: move burst egress through dedicated NAT pool, split SNAT duties across 4 appliances, and use SNAT port reuse + ephemeral port mapping on hosts to avoid exhaustion.
- Cache warmup: maintain a rolling mini-cache (hot KV shard) on the burst ring that mirrors baseline's top N prompts; use a short wavefront warmup on scale events (~30s).

Concrete sizing & assumptions (we should validate numbers with those traces):
- Baseline capacity: assume each A100-equivalent host sustains ~1k tokens/sec for our mixed model under tuned batching. To hit 350 tokens/sec sustained with 99th <400ms, plan for 1 host as baseline minimum plus safety margin -> provision 2 baseline hosts (sustained headroom ~2k tps).
- Burst ring: to cover up to 10x spikes (3.5k tokens/sec) we recommend an additional 4 hosts pre-warmed (burst ring capacity ~4k tps). Burst ring kept in partial power state with model loaded and warm KV.
- Admission control: implement token-based gating: at 90% baseline capacity, redirect new sessions to the burst ring. If burst ring reaches 85%, switch to graceful degradation (priority requests only, truncated responses).

Network and SNAT plan:
- Create a dedicated NAT cluster for the burst ring (2 appliances active, 1 standby) with 3x SNAT capacity to avoid port exhaustion. Configure per-host ephemeral port range and reuse time = 30s.
- Prefer local rack placement for burst hosts to avoid cross-rack egress; if not possible, limit simultaneous burst scale-ups per rack to avoid hitting 25Gbps leaf.

Warmup recipe:
1) Maintain a small hot list (top 500 prefixes) mirrored to burst ring via a 15s async sync.
2) On scale event, begin a wavewarm: 5 warmup requests per host prioritized by KV locality (~30s to reach steady P50).
3) If traffic continues to ramp beyond expected window, automatically spin additional ephemeral hosts (cold) but keep them behind a queue to protect tail latency.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Can your team confirm the observed peak tokens/sec in the CSV (columns noted in the attachment)? We based the host assumptions on rough 1k tps per host; if your models are heavier, we need to adjust.
- Permissible fail modes: is truncation acceptable at 15–20% completeness during extreme bursts?

Proposed schedule:
- Wed 5/19: 30m working session with your ops to validate traffic numbers and rack map.
- Fri 5/21: deliver a 1-page provisioning plan + runbook for ops + a cost estimate.

I’ll loop Jonas for networking specifics and Laura for SLA wording.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-18T13:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — baseline vs spikes (Q1 load samples attached)

Beth/Karthik — network detail follow-up. Quick notes from infra review: 

1) Egress per host: with 25Gbps leaf uplinks we should budget 18Gbps usable (allowing for overhead). If your bursts have many parallel small requests (low tokens per request), SNAT port usage will be the gating factor before raw bandwidth.
2) SNAT strategy: we can do a matrix: (num_hosts * ephemeral_ports_per_host) + NAT_ports >= estimated concurrent outbound flows. For safety, target 2.5x the observed concurrent flows in CSV.
3) Cross-rack mitigation: implement a rack-aware admission controller that limits how many burst replicas come up in a single rack in a 60s window. Simple heuristic: max 2 new burst hosts per rack per minute.

Operational hooks to add to runbook:
- Pre-burst checklist: confirm KV mirror sync, verify NAT appliance health, confirm disk-backed caching warmed for top embeddings.
- Post-burst audit: collect DB of dropped requests, SNAT port utilization snapshot, and token latency histogram.

I'll prepare a short network appendix that details port math and NAT sizing.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good and actionable. A few clarifications from ops after a quick pass: 

- The CSV peak shows ~4.2k concurrent flows during the largest spike, not 3.5k (our earlier memory was off).
- Truncation at 15% completeness is acceptable for non-logged-in discovery traffic, but not for authenticated support flow (we have tagging to mark priority).

Can we adjust burst ring to 5 pre-warmed hosts (to hit ~5k tps buffer with your 1k tps host assumption) and keep admission control rules to preserve priority-tagged sessions? If yes we'll approve the runbook and schedule the pilot next week.

Also please include a short checklist for Ops to validate NAT port headroom before and after the pilot.

Best,
Beth
